provenance.notes: Commit cb09e8f (2026-09-27) contains the validated NBM production-readiness code (data/nbm.py, data/weather_state.py's completeness fix, the pre-production benchmark/validation findings) but scripts/pilot_phase5_nbm.py at that commit still had its deliberate launch guard (main() raised RuntimeError) and no production launch driver. Immediately before launch, an UNCOMMITTED change to scripts/pilot_phase5_nbm.py removed that guard and added the production run_times_for_selected_days()/main()/write_report() driver (mirroring pilot_phase4_gfs.py's structure) -- the extraction logic itself (extract_one_run_hour, required_forecast_hours_for_run) was already validated at commit cb09e8f and unchanged. That same script change is committed together with this manifest, so as of the commit accompanying this manifest, the entire 31,578-item dataset is reproducible from a single commit's code going forward. Separately: the extraction run's output directory (data/processed/pilot/nbm/) was found to contain 9 stray checkpoint entries / 648 rows left over from an earlier production-readiness validation-phase small sample (12 items) that had written into the same path before this launch. This was detected during the post-run integrity audit (checkpoint had 31,587 keys vs. 31,578 planned), traced, and cleaned before this manifest was generated: the 648 out-of-scope rows were removed from the one affected Parquet part, the 9 stray checkpoint keys were deleted, and the checkpoint/persisted-row reconciliation was re-verified to match exactly. 7 of the 31,578 real pilot items also failed on the first pass with transient S3 ConnectionResetError (identical pattern to HRRR/GFS's transient failures); all 7 were retried successfully using the unmodified production extraction path with 0 further failures.

source.name: nbm
source.fh0_semantics: forecast_hour=0 does not exist for NBM at all (confirmed 404 at every run hour/date tested, and 0 rows observed at forecast_hour=0 in the final dataset) -- there is no degenerate F0 message to special-case, unlike HRRR/GFS.
source.run_hour_schedule: 3-tier schedule keyed by run_hour % 6 (full/medium/short horizons) -- see data.nbm.nbm_schedule_tier() and docs/nbm_pilot_readiness.md. Extraction is target-day-only (bounded by each selected day's UTC window), so observed per-run max forecast_hour in this dataset is well below each tier's theoretical ceiling (F264/F189/F36) by design.
source.apcp_6h_semantics: present only when valid_time's hour is an absolute UTC synoptic hour (00/06/12/18Z), i.e. (run_hour+forecast_hour) % 6 == 0 -- NOT simply forecast_hour % 6 == 0. Verified at full production scale: 40,158/40,158 APCP_6H rows have valid_time.hour % 6 == 0.
source.tmax_tmin_semantics: TMAX_PERIOD/TMIN_PERIOD extracted only for run_hour in {0, 12} (verified: only these two run hours appear among TMAX/TMIN rows). Period is fully reconstructable as [valid_time - temporal_window_hours, valid_time] (temporal_window_hours=12 for both).

contamination_removed.source: leftover from an earlier 12-item production-readiness validation sample that wrote into the same output directory before this launch

runtime_overrides.note: matches scripts/pilot_phase5_nbm.py's own committed default (independently benchmarked for NBM, see docs/nbm_pilot_readiness.md section 17) -- no override needed

performance.estimate_vs_actual_note: Pre-launch estimates (docs/nbm_pilot_readiness.md section 17, from a 20-item benchmark sample) were ~314 GB remote / ~32 MB local / ~5.3h runtime. Actual full-scale production run: ~316.0 GB remote (close match), ~28.0 MB local (close match, slightly lower due to real variable-presence mix), ~3.68h runtime (faster than estimated -- the benchmark's repeated-short-trial overhead did not reflect a long sustained run's steady-state throughput, which held at ~2.39 items/sec vs. the benchmark's 1.66-1.82 items/sec).
